belief: Addiction is a treatable disease and the cycle can be broken — and our clients can be empowered to take responsibility for their own ongoing recovery.
heroQuote: Where hope in life is rekindled.
aboutParas: We are a fully registered, NACADA-accredited addiction recovery centre, known for breaking the cycle of addiction and restoring health to individuals, families and whole communities.

Every member of staff shares one belief: addiction is a treatable disease, and recovery heals the mind, body and spirit together. So treatment here is medical, psychological, spiritual and holistic — because we are treating a person, not a habit.

Your culture, your family and your values sit at the centre of your recovery. Our whole structure — the facility, the wholesome food, the loving staff — exists to make it safe for you to speak honestly.
familyBody: We run a comprehensive three-day programme for family and friends. It teaches you how to stop taking part in unhealthy patterns, how to set boundaries that hold, and how to support recovery without losing yourself.

marks.title: Impaired control
marks.body: Using more, or for longer, than intended — and being unable to cut down.

marks.title: Compulsive use
marks.body: Obtaining or using becomes the primary focus of the day.

marks.title: Continued use despite harm
marks.body: Persisting through physical, psychological, social and financial damage.

marks.title: Risky use
marks.body: Using in hazardous situations, ignoring a high risk of personal harm.

vision: A healthy society free from addictions.
heroBadges: Staff who have walked this road
aboutTitle: A therapeutic community, not an institution.
mission: Professional treatment and rehabilitation of persons with substance use disorders.
diseaseNote: Classified as a chronic brain disorder by the American Society of Addiction Medicine and the National Institute on Drug Abuse.

aboutSlides.alt: A group of hands holding one another

treatmentIntro: Detox alone is not treatment. Each stage hands you to the next, and none of it ends at discharge.
familyTitle: The disease affects the whole family. So does the healing.

testimonials.quote: The attitude of the staff is warm and welcoming. I can share openly here, and everyone is willing to give me feedback.
The programme has saved my life. My sessions brought out things I truly believed I would never tell a soul.
I was very happy with the openness and honesty I felt in the group. It made it safe to talk about our struggles.

programmesIntro: Long enough to build a life that holds. Every case is assessed on admission and the plan is tailored — these are the programmes we run.

signs.label: Loss of control
signs.hint: Cannot stop or limit use, even after trying

signs.label: Preoccupation
signs.hint: Constant focus on getting, using or recovering

signs.label: Neglected duties
signs.hint: Work, school or home obligations slipping

signs.label: Loss of interest
signs.hint: Hobbies, sport and friends given up

signs.label: Tolerance
signs.hint: Needing more, or more often, for the same effect

signs.label: Withdrawal
signs.hint: Shaking, sweating, nausea or anxiety when stopping

signs.label: Sleep and appetite
signs.hint: Sudden weight change, insomnia, odd hours

signs.label: Appearance
signs.hint: Noticeable decline in hygiene and grooming

signs.label: Risky behaviour
signs.hint: Driving impaired or using in unsafe places

signs.label: Physical clues
signs.hint: Bloodshot or glassy eyes, unusual pupils, slurred speech, poor coordination

heroBody: Promises Treatment Centre is a residential home for recovery from alcohol and drug addiction. Safe, confidential and affordable — and many of the people who will care for you have walked this road themselves.
diseaseTitle: Yes. And that changes everything about how we treat you.
quote: Rarely have we seen a person fail who has thoroughly followed our path.

faqs.a: Alcohol dependence is a three-month residential programme and hard drugs or narcotics is six months. Relapse is two months, expelled students one month, and suspended students two weeks. Every case is assessed on admission and matched to the right programme.

Our costs are deliberately reasonable and treatment services are tailor-made for each case, so the figure depends on the programme. Call us and we will be straight with you about what your situation would involve.
Admission is available to all suitable clients irrespective of race, ethnicity, gender, culture, ideology, political or religious beliefs, sexual orientation, language and HIV status.

Yes, and we encourage it. We run a comprehensive three-day family therapy programme for family and friends of our clients — it restores broken relationships, teaches healthy boundaries, and makes long-term recovery far more likely.

faqs.q: Is detox enough on its own?
faqs.a: No. Detox manages withdrawal and addresses physical dependence, but detox with no follow-up is not treatment. The psychological side has to be treated too, through counselling, group work and a residential programme.
Relapse happens, even to the most dedicated people in recovery, and it is not the end of anything. Do not wait for it to get worse — contact us immediately and we will pick up where we left off.

services.title: Detoxification
services.body: A medically supervised process to clear the substance while withdrawal is managed. Days to a few weeks, depending on the substance and the severity of dependence.

services.title: Alcohol & drug treatment
services.body: Residential care combining medication-assisted treatment, daily group therapy, one-to-one counselling and a structured routine that rebuilds healthy habits.

services.title: Family therapy
services.body: A three-day programme for family and friends. It replaces negative patterns with positive ones, sets healthy boundaries and repairs what addiction damaged.

services.title: Aftercare & outreach
services.body: Follow-up on discharged clients, support-group placement and continued therapy to prevent relapse — plus community outreach on substance misuse.

diseaseBody: Repeated use floods the brain with dopamine. In time the brain stops making normal amounts on its own, so the substance is prioritised over everything that once mattered — and going without brings real physical pain. This is a chronic, treatable medical condition, not a failure of character.
heroTitle: You have not lost yourself. You have only lost your way.
